correctness.rationale: The one-step matrix A(h) sends (q,p) to ((1-h^2)q+hp,-hq+p). At constant h, the form q^2-hqp+p^2 is invariant and positive definite for 0<h<2. For the random case, expand the quadratic action on (q^2,qp,p^2), then average independently of the incoming state. Direct expansion of the three-by-three determinant at 1 gives -2(m1^2 m4-2 m1 m2 m3+m2^3); the latter bracket is E[(m1 H^2-m2 H)^2]. It is strictly positive for a non-point distribution because H>0 almost surely. The monic real characteristic polynomial is negative at 1 and positive at large positive arguments, so the covariance spectral radius rho exceeds 1. The positive-map cone theorem supplies a nonzero PSD adjoint eigenmatrix P at rho. If P is rank one, write P=vv^T and test on a real w perpendicular to v, giving E[(v^T A(H)w)^2]=0, hence a real invariant line for A(H)^T almost surely. This is impossible because the discriminant is h^2(h^2-4)<0. P is thus positive definite; iteration of its eigenform gives both upper and lower rho^k comparisons for every starting direction. Neither the computation nor the definiteness argument requires the law to stay away from 0 or 2. Including 0 would invalidate the nondegeneracy argument for a mixture of 0 and one fixed positive step. Replay: RESULT.md lines 23–78; verify.py lines 8–60 was inspected without execution. Its symbolic and rational tests are not the proof of the all-law spectral implication.

value.rationale: The universal instability question is scientifically meaningful, but its useful classification and exact rate characterization are already available. The residual determinant-at-one identity is a short alternate sign proof by expanding the available three-dimensional transfer, not a new growth estimate, stability boundary or independently needed exact invariant. The scalar identity and identical two-point witness do not justify a standalone repair.
